title: Animated image formats as paint clocks
blurb: Ten animated images as canvas children: GIF, APNG, WebP, AVIF, three SVG files, an inline SVG, a CSS background and a GIF that plays once. Each one swings a sign by one step for each paint event it raises, so a format that raises one event per frame keeps its sign in step with the others.
question: Which animated image formats raise paint once per frame when the image is a child of a drawable canvas?
result: All that were tried, in Chromium 157: GIF, APNG, WebP and AVIF, SVG with stepped SMIL or CSS animation, inline SVG, a CSS background image, <picture>, <object> and content: url() each raised 12.5 events a second for 12.5 frames a second. A continuous SMIL animation raised one per display frame. A GIF that plays once stopped raising them after its last frame. An SVG file in an <img> stopped when the place it was drawn at left the window, and the raster formats did not.
